explanations: transfer() locks the sender, then the receiver. When alice pays bob while bob pays alice, the first transfer holds alice's lock and waits for bob's, and the second holds bob's and waits for alice's. Neither ever releases (a lock-ordering deadlock). The fix acquires both locks in one global order, here sorted by wallet ID, no matter which way the money moves. Every transfer then waits for locks in the same sequence and a cycle can't form. Reading the balances after both locks are held also keeps the check-then-write atomic.
